plan: This is a second-price auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid), which is strategically equivalent to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others bid, since you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and pay that second-highest bid, which is independent of your own bid choice. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to you; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, my optimal strategy is to bid exactly my value of $19.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you only pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Overbidding risks winning at a loss, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $44, bidding exactly $44 ensures I capture positive expected profit whenever the second-highest bid is below my value, without risk of overpaying.

In a second-price auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Since I don't gain from bidding above or below my valuation of $43, the optimal action is to bid exactly $43. This ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and avoid overpaying.
